title: Automate hooks/pre-commit installation instead of relying on manual copy/chmod instructions
why: The pre-commit hook only runs if a contributor manually copies it into .git/hooks/ — there is no `make install-hooks`/`setup` target anywhere in either Makefile that does this for them, confirmed by grepping both Makefiles for 'hook' and finding no match. This repo's own `.git/hooks/pre-commit` is absent right now, empirically confirming the gate is not installed even in the reference checkout. CI backstops the same two checks (format/analyze), so this is not a silent-corruption risk, but it means every new contributor's first several commits get zero local pre-commit feedback and the guardrail is bypassable by simply never running the two setup lines — exactly the 'check that can never fire by default' pattern this audit area was asked to hunt.
recommendation: Add a `make install-hooks` target (or a postinstall step referenced from the top-level setup docs) that performs the cp+chmod, and reference it from hooks/README.md/CONTRIBUTING.md instead of raw shell steps.
acceptance_criteria: A committed make/tool target installs hooks/pre-commit into .git/hooks/ without manual copy-paste.
hooks/README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, learning_tracker/README.md, and docs/development-guide.md point to that target.
